summaryEn: Elon Musk's 2009 sit-down with Charlie Rose: leaving South Africa, co-founding PayPal, and the high-stakes early years of Tesla Motors and SpaceX during the financial crisis.
summaryZh: 埃隆·马斯克在2009年与查理·罗斯的对谈：离开南非、共同创办 PayPal，以及金融危机期间 Tesla Motors 和 SpaceX 风险重重的早期岁月。

segments.textEn: Elon Musk is here. He is chief executive of two startup companies with bold missions. He leads Tesla Motors, the electric car company that has attracted attention from both car enthusiasts and environmentalists as well. The company's powerful roadster, which can travel from 0 to 60 in less than 4 seconds, is entirely powered by batteries. The company plans to break into the mainstream auto market with an electric sedan as early as 2011.
segments.textZh: 埃隆·马斯克来到这里。他是2家使命宏大的初创公司的首席执行官。他领导着电动汽车公司 Tesla Motors，这家公司既吸引了汽车爱好者的关注，也吸引了环保人士的关注。该公司动力强劲的 Roadster 完全由电池驱动，从0加速到60不到4秒。该公司计划最早于2011年凭借一款电动轿车打入主流汽车市场。

segments.textEn: Musk is also founder and CEO of Space Exploration Technologies, a company trying to slash the cost of space travel. Last year, the company signed an agreement with NASA to send cargo to the International Space Station. And if that is not enough, he's also chairman of a growing company called SolarCity that installs solar panels on homes and businesses. He has thrived in Silicon Valley, one of the co founders of PayPal, the online payments company that eBay bought for $1.5 billion in 2002.
segments.textZh: 马斯克还是太空探索技术公司的创始人兼首席执行官，这家公司正试图大幅降低太空旅行的成本。去年，该公司与 NASA 签署了一项协议，向国际空间站运送货物。如果这还不够，他还是一家名为 SolarCity、正在不断发展的公司的董事长，该公司为住宅和企业安装太阳能电池板。他在硅谷发展得很成功，是在线支付公司 PayPal 的联合创始人之一，eBay 于2002年以15亿美元收购了该公司。

segments.textEn: I am pleased to have him here at this table for the first time. Welcome.
segments.textZh: 我很高兴第一次请他来到这张桌前。欢迎。

segments.textEn: Thank you. Thanks for having me. I've been a big fan of the show for a long time.
segments.textZh: 谢谢。感谢邀请我来。很长时间以来，我一直是这个节目的忠实观众。

segments.textEn: Let's just talk about you first so that if the audience does not know. Growing up in South Africa.
segments.textZh: 我们先谈谈你，这样如果观众还不了解的话。在南非长大。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 对。

segments.textEn: And how did you end up in Canada?
segments.textZh: 那你最后是怎么到了加拿大？

segments.textEn: Well, I guess growing up in South Africa, I was actually. It was very technology oriented. And I taught myself how to program computers, mostly because I wanted to program games. And I, when I was about 12, I programmed, sold my first game. And whenever I'd read about technology and great innovation, it was coming from the United States. And so that's where I wanted to be. And I tried to convince my parents to move there and neither of them would, they were divorced.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我想，在南非长大的时候，我其实。当时非常以技术为导向。我自学了如何给计算机编程，主要是因为我想编写游戏。我，我大约12岁的时候，编写并卖掉了自己的第1个游戏。每当我读到有关技术和伟大创新的内容时，它们都来自美国。所以那就是我想去的地方。我试着说服父母搬到那里，但他们谁都不愿意，他们离婚了。

segments.textEn: I tried to. My mother, neither would do it. My mother later moved back to initially Canada and then the U.S. and so when I was 17, as soon as I got my Canadian passport, three weeks later, I was in Canada.
segments.textZh: 我试过。我母亲，他们谁都不愿意。后来我母亲搬了回去，先是加拿大，然后是美国，所以我17岁时，一拿到加拿大护照，3周后，我就在加拿大了。

segments.textEn: So here you are, and you come to Canada and make it to the United States, and then you and several other guys come together and create PayPal and you sell it to eBay for one point, whatever it was. $5 billion.
segments.textZh: 所以你到了这里，你来到加拿大，又成功去了美国，然后你和另外几个家伙走到一起创办了 PayPal，又以1点几，具体是多少来着。50亿美元卖给了 eBay。

segments.textEn: Yeah. So after PayPal, that gave me a fair bit of capital.
segments.textZh: 对。所以在 PayPal 之后，那给了我相当多的资本。

segments.textEn: And there were three areas. When I was in college, there were three areas that I thought would most affect the future of humanity, and those were the Internet, the transition to a sustainable energy and transportation sector. And the third was space exploration. In particular, the extension of life to multiple planets. Now, I didn't ever expect to be involved in the third one, but that seemed to me that's something that would be very important for the future.
segments.textZh: 当时有3个领域。我上大学时，有3个领域是我认为会对人类未来产生最大影响的，它们是互联网、向可持续能源和交通运输领域的转型。第3个是太空探索。尤其是将生命扩展到多个行星。那时，我从未料到自己会参与第3个领域，但在我看来，那似乎是对未来非常重要的事情。

segments.textEn: And with the capital I got from the sale of PayPal, I was able to go into both those areas.
segments.textZh: 凭借出售 PayPal 所获得的资本，我得以进入那2个领域。

segments.textEn: And so hence SpaceX and in the space and then in the sustainable energy and transportation, you've got SolarCity and Tesla.
segments.textZh: 所以因此，在太空领域有 SpaceX，然后在可持续能源和交通运输领域，你有 SolarCity 和 Tesla。

segments.textEn: Let me talk about space exploration just for a moment. How is it going in terms of creating the systems that will engage us in space exploration, not just for governments and not just for NASA, but for private citizens as well?
segments.textZh: 让我先花一点时间谈谈太空探索。在创建让我们参与太空探索的系统方面，目前进展如何，不仅面向政府、不仅面向 NASA，也面向普通公民？

segments.textEn: Well, you have to divide the efforts that are going on into what is an orbit class effort versus a suborbital class effort. And there's really a very big difference. But, but the general public doesn't understand the difference between getting to space and getting to orbit. And so it's important to make that distinction. To do a suborbital flight, you need a terminal velocity of around Mach 3. To get to orbit you need a terminal velocity of Mach 25.
segments.textZh: 嗯，你必须把目前进行的工作分为轨道级工作和亚轨道级工作。两者确实有非常大的区别。但，但是普通公众不了解进入太空和进入轨道之间的区别。所以作出这种区分很重要。要进行亚轨道飞行，你需要达到大约3马赫的最终速度。要进入轨道，你需要达到25马赫的最终速度。

segments.textEn: It's a huge, huge difference because the energy required to do that scales with the square of the velocity. So suborbital might be 9 units of energy. Orbit is 625 units of energy. So it's only about 1.5% of the energy of orbit is required to get to suborbit. So there's a number of efforts in the suborbital category that certainly could grow one day to orbital. There's Jeff Bezos has an effort and I know that's something that's really.
segments.textZh: 这是一个巨大、巨大的差异，因为做到这一点所需的能量随速度的平方变化。所以亚轨道飞行可能需要9个单位的能量。轨道飞行需要625个单位的能量。所以到达亚轨道所需的能量只有到达轨道所需能量的大约1.5%。因此，亚轨道类别中有许多项目，有朝一日当然可能发展到轨道级。杰夫·贝索斯有一个项目，我知道那确实是某种。

segments.textEn: Is Branson involved in this or not?
segments.textZh: 布兰森参与了这件事，还是没有？

segments.textEn: Yes, Branson, absolutely. Not so much directly from the technology standpoint, but from his. He's funding that development at Scaled Composites in California.
segments.textZh: 是的，布兰森，当然参与了。从技术角度来说，他没有那么直接参与，而是通过他的。他正在资助加利福尼亚州 Scaled Composites 的那项开发工作。

segments.textEn: And what are you doing?
segments.textZh: 那你在做什么？

segments.textEn: So we're in the orbit class and it's a lot more capital and that's really where you're sort of pushing the ragged edge of what's physically possible. And last year we got to orbit for the first time with our rocket and that was certainly a huge relief and a milestone.
segments.textZh: 所以我们属于轨道级，需要的资本多得多，而那确实是你在某种程度上逼近物理可行性极限的地方。去年，我们的火箭第一次进入了轨道，那当然让人如释重负，也是一个里程碑。

segments.textEn: And so what's the next step? You get a rocket into orbit. Yeah.
segments.textZh: 那么下一步是什么？你把一枚火箭送入轨道。对。

segments.textEn: So next month we are putting a satellite for Malaysia into orbit and then from Malaysia. For Malaysia. For Malaysia, yes, the Malaysian satellite. But in the rocket business, the rocket company does the launch. It's not like the airline business. So you don't sell the rocket, you sell the launch.
segments.textZh: 所以下个月，我们将把马来西亚的一颗卫星送入轨道，然后从马来西亚。为马来西亚。为马来西亚，是的，马来西亚的卫星。但在火箭业务中，是火箭公司执行发射。它不像航空业务。所以你不是出售火箭，而是出售发射服务。

segments.textEn: And then later this year we'll be launching our big rocket from Cape Canaveral. That's the Falcon 9 and that's the one that's going to be servicing the space station among other things.
segments.textZh: 然后今年晚些时候，我们将在卡纳维拉尔角发射大型火箭。那就是猎鹰9号，它将承担为空间站提供服务等任务。

segments.textEn: Is there a philosophy here that somehow the private sector can do a lot more than it has done in areas that seem. Because of the size reserved for government?
segments.textZh: 这里是否有这样一种理念，即私营部门能够在一些领域做得比过去多得多，而那些领域似乎。因为其规模而一直是政府专属的？

segments.textEn: Yeah, definitely. The private sector is very good at optimization and innovation. I mean, private sector is generally better at doing things than the government, I think that's fair to say. But, you know, there are certain things that the government that are suited to the government, like basic research and that sort of thing.
segments.textZh: 对，当然。私营部门非常擅长优化和创新。我的意思是，私营部门做事情通常比政府更出色，我认为这么说是公平的。但是，你知道，有些事情政府，适合由政府来做，比如基础研究之类的事情。

segments.textEn: But
segments.textZh: 但是

segments.textEn: yeah. So as far as SpaceX, the reason that there hasn't been a huge number of a big improvement in the space industry, I think, is because of it's very difficult for SHINPA to create a destruction process to come into effect because there's such a significant amount of capital that's needed to start a rocket company. And it's a very difficult technical challenge. And the number of people that really understand rocketry in the world is a very small number.
segments.textZh: 是的。所以就 SpaceX 而言，太空产业一直没有出现数量巨大的重大改进，我认为原因是，SHINPA 很难创造出一个破坏过程并使其生效，因为创办一家火箭公司需要极其庞大的资本。而且这是一项非常困难的技术挑战。世界上真正了解火箭技术的人数量非常少。

segments.textEn: So it's really huge barriers to entry. And that's why we haven't seen the forcing function of improvement that there should have been over the years.
segments.textZh: 所以进入壁垒确实极其高。这就是为什么多年来，我们一直没有看到本应出现的那种推动改进的强制力量。

segments.textEn: And your understanding came from sort of. This was not what you studied in college?
segments.textZh: 而你的理解大概来自。这不是你在大学里学的东西？

segments.textEn: Well, I studied physics.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我学过物理学。

segments.textEn: Well, studying physics and studying rocket science.
segments.textZh: 嗯，学习物理学和学习火箭科学。

segments.textEn: Yeah. No, it gives you the basics. Gives you the basics. Good framework, Good analytical framework.
segments.textZh: 是的。不，它会给你基础。给你基础。很好的框架，很好的分析框架。

segments.textEn: But no, I picked it up along the way.
segments.textZh: 但不是，我是一路上学会的。

segments.textEn: What is your core competence? You think you.
segments.textZh: 你的核心能力是什么？你认为你。

segments.textEn: I think it's technology. Technology, yeah, technology. If something has to be designed and invented and you have to figure out how to ensure that the value of the thing you create is greater than the cost of the inputs, then that's probably my core skill.
segments.textZh: 我认为是技术。技术，是的，技术。如果某样东西必须被设计和发明，而你必须弄清楚如何确保你创造的东西的价值大于投入成本，那么这大概就是我的核心技能。

segments.textEn: Now, bring me to the car. I drove a car this afternoon. So far, so good, which was terrific. It's the roadster. Where does that stand you? Obviously, I've been in the Google parking lot.
segments.textZh: 现在，带我谈谈这辆车。我今天下午开了一辆车。目前为止，一切顺利，那非常棒。是 Roadster。你目前进展到什么程度？显然，我去过 Google 的停车场。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: Okay.
segments.textZh: 好的。

segments.textEn: You've seen a few there, I've seen
segments.textZh: 你在那里见过几辆，我见过

segments.textEn: a few there, yeah. I'm sure that's true in other places in Silicon Valley. I don't know whether it's particularly a car that appeals to people in Silicon Valley because of interest in technology and high performance and lots of other things, or what, whether there are a lot of rich people who are willing to spend that kind of money for something they think is on the cutting edge of causes they believe in sustainable energy.
segments.textZh: 在那里见过几辆，是的。我相信硅谷其他地方也是如此。我不知道这是不是一款特别吸引硅谷人士的车，因为他们对技术、高性能和许多其他东西感兴趣，还是怎么回事，是否有很多富人愿意花那种钱，购买他们认为处于自己所信奉的事业前沿的东西，也就是可持续能源。

segments.textEn: Tell me about where you are in this development of this electric car which has most of all this extraordinary sort of power.
segments.textZh: 跟我讲讲你们在研发这款电动汽车方面进展到哪里了，它最突出的就是这种非凡的动力。

segments.textEn: Yeah, zero to 60 time at 3.9 segments.
segments.textZh: 是的，零到60的时间是3.9段。

segments.textEn: This is extraordinary when you think about sports cars and anything else that's out on the road today.
segments.textZh: 当你想到跑车和如今道路上的其他任何车辆时，这都非同寻常。

segments.textEn: Yeah. In fact, on the Top Gear test track, our standard roadster beats a Porsche GT3. Exactly. Which is.
segments.textZh: 是的。事实上，在 Top Gear 测试赛道上，我们的标准版 Roadster 击败了一辆 Porsche GT3。没错。也就是。

segments.textEn: That's a replica.
segments.textZh: 那是一辆复制品。

segments.textEn: And the Roadster Sport will be even better.
segments.textZh: 而 Roadster Sport 还会更好。

segments.textEn: But you've also said in terms of where you want to go, that developing a high performance sports car is not what this is about.
segments.textZh: 但关于你想走向何方，你也说过，研发高性能跑车并不是这件事的目的。

segments.textEn: Absolutely.
segments.textZh: 绝对是。

segments.textEn: This is about something else. And you want to develop a sedan.
segments.textZh: 这是为了别的事情。而且你想开发一款轿车。

segments.textEn: Yeah. The whole purpose behind Tesla, the reason I put so much of my time and money into helping create the business is we want to serve as a catalyst for accelerating the electric car revolution.
segments.textZh: 对。Tesla 背后的全部目的，也是我投入如此多时间和金钱来帮助创建这家公司的原因，就是我们希望充当催化剂，加速电动汽车革命。

segments.textEn: The price of gas at the pump does not reflect the true cost of gasoline because you have a consumption of a public good. It's one of the most. It's really a common problem in economics. You have the same thing in fishing, where because there's no cost to fishing stocks, people just overfish and you have disaster that ensues. And here we're not paying for the cost of the CO2 concentration in the oceans and atmospheres, we're not paying for all these, the ancillary effects of wars and all the other things at the gas pump.
segments.textZh: 加油站的汽油价格并未反映汽油的真实成本，因为你消耗了一种公共物品。这是最……这其实是经济学中的一个常见问题。渔业中也存在同样的情况，因为捕捞鱼类种群没有成本，人们就会过度捕捞，随后灾难便会发生。而在这里，我们没有为海洋和大气中二氧化碳浓度的成本付费，也没有在加油站为所有这些、战争的附带影响以及其他一切付费。

segments.textEn: So you effectively have a subsidy taking place at the gas pump because of that. So the only way to bridge that is with innovation, is to try to try to make electric cars better sooner than they would otherwise be.
segments.textZh: 所以，实际上正因为如此，加油站存在一种补贴。因此，弥合这一差距的唯一办法就是创新，就是努力、努力让电动汽车比原本能够达到的时间更早变得更好。

segments.textEn: Now, suppose this, this is a hypothetical which may or may not speak to the point. But suppose 15 years ago, right. Let's say Bill Clinton as president, who talked about the road to the 21st century and all of that. Suppose he had said, I believe so much in sustainable energy that I want to make a commitment. And the federal government, using all of its resources, will develop an electric car with appropriate battery power that will change the face of automobile, the automobile industry in the world.
segments.textZh: 现在，假设这样，这只是一个可能切中要点、也可能没有的假设。但假设在15年前，对吧。比如说，比尔·克林顿担任总统时，他谈到了通往21世纪的道路以及所有那些事情。假设他说，我如此相信可持续能源，以至于我想作出承诺。而联邦政府将动用其全部资源，开发一款配备适当电池动力的电动汽车，它将改变汽车、改变世界汽车工业的面貌。

segments.textEn: Was that very doable? Bill Clinton was elected in 1992, 17 years ago.
segments.textZh: 那非常可行吗？比尔·克林顿于1992年当选，那是17年前。

segments.textEn: Yeah. You could have made a reasonably good electric car around that time for a lot of investment.
segments.textZh: 是的。在那个时候，投入大量资金，你本可以造出一款相当不错的电动汽车。

segments.textEn: And should that have been done, should the US Government have made that kind of change? Otherwise you will not be able to change the driving habits of Americans.
segments.textZh: 那是否本该去做，美国政府是否本该推动那种改变？否则你就无法改变美国人的驾驶习惯。

segments.textEn: Was it a worthwhile expenditure at that time?
segments.textZh: 在当时，那是一笔值得的支出吗？

segments.textEn: I think it probably would have been a worthwhile expenditure. But the thing that really helps electric cars is lithium ion.
segments.textZh: 我认为那很可能会是一笔值得的支出。但真正对电动汽车有帮助的是锂离子。

segments.textEn: Right. And when did that come around? I mean, explain why batteries has always been the great dilemma for developing an electric car.
segments.textZh: 对。那是什么时候出现的？我的意思是，解释一下为什么电池一直是开发电动汽车的一大难题。

segments.textEn: Sure. Well, the energy contained within a battery is so much less than is contained in gasoline that, I mean, it's really almost. It's hard to quite describe. Another way to put it is the Tesla battery pack in the Roadster, which is the most advanced battery pack in the world. The common reference is to call what is actually a cell a battery. So a cell is the little single can of chemicals, and then if you have multiple cells, that's what actually battery.
segments.textZh: 当然。嗯，电池中所含的能量比汽油中所含的少得多，我的意思是，这真的几乎。很难准确描述。换一种说法，Roadster里的Tesla电池包，是世界上最先进的电池包。通常人们会把实际上是电芯的东西称为电池。所以，电芯就是装有化学物质的单个小罐子，然后如果你有多个电芯，那才实际上是电池。

segments.textEn: That's literally what a battery means.
segments.textZh: 这就是电池这个词的字面含义。

segments.textEn: Multiple cells.
segments.textZh: 多个电芯。

segments.textEn: Multiple cells. And as the batteries get bigger and bigger, they get harder and harder to deal with. So the cell that we use is a commodity cell.
segments.textZh: 多个电芯。而且随着电池变得越来越大，它们也变得越来越难以处理。所以我们使用的电芯是一种商品化电芯。

segments.textEn: You can buy it anywhere, pretty much.
segments.textZh: 你几乎可以在任何地方买到它。

segments.textEn: And it's the same sort of thing that's in any one number of laptops. The challenge is combining those cells into. And having thousands of them, making sure they're safe, making sure they'll last for 200,000 miles or 100,000 over bumps and potholes and extremes of temperature and safe in a crash. That compounds the problem massively. And you've got to make sure the charges and temperature is balanced across the whole thing.
segments.textZh: 而且它与许多笔记本电脑里装的是同一类东西。挑战在于把这些电芯组合成。并且拥有数千个电芯，要确保它们安全，确保它们能使用200,000英里，或者100,000，经历颠簸、坑洞和极端温度，并且在碰撞中安全。这极大地加剧了问题。而且你必须确保整个电池包的电量和温度保持均衡。

segments.textZh: 是的。拉里和谢尔盖都是 Tesla 的投资者

segments.textEn: and they drive them or don't drive them.
segments.textZh: 而且他们开这些车，还是不开。

segments.textEn: Yeah, they drive them, absolutely.
segments.textZh: 对，他们开，当然。

segments.textEn: Because some of the criticism that comes at you and the company now is that you went out to seek a lot of external financing and did not reach your goals.
segments.textZh: 因为现在针对你和公司的批评中，有一些是说你曾四处寻求大量外部融资，却没有达到目标。

segments.textEn: Well, it's taking us longer to reach our goals, but we are definitely.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我们实现目标花的时间更长，但我们肯定会。

segments.textEn: What was it? Raise 100 million to raise 40 or what was the goal?
segments.textZh: 当时是什么？募集1亿美元来筹集4000万，还是目标是什么？

segments.textEn: Well, I think some of the stumbles were silly mistakes we made ourselves. Some of them were market externalities and we were getting ready to raise, or we're in the process of raising about $100 million round that began in sort of the summer of last year. And then Ran into, you know, force five hurricane.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我认为有些磕绊是我们自己犯下的愚蠢错误。有些是市场外部因素，而我们当时正准备募集，或者说正在进行一轮约1亿美元的融资，这轮融资大约始于去年夏天。然后就遭遇了，你知道，5级飓风。

segments.textEn: An economic circumstance that took everything inside.
segments.textZh: 一种把一切都卷入其中的经济局势。

segments.textEn: Yeah. And so that forced us to scale back our plans a little bit. We had to do a layoff and we had to raise the money internally from existing investors. I had to put up a lot of the money personally and there was just no money. And so that was, it was sort of a hair raising time for the company. But at this point we're actually in good shape. We expect to be profitable in the third quarter.
segments.textZh: 对。所以那迫使我们稍微缩减了计划。我们不得不裁员，而且不得不从现有投资者那里内部筹集资金。我个人不得不拿出很大一笔钱，而当时就是没有钱。所以那是，那对公司来说算是一段令人胆战心惊的时期。但到目前这个时候，我们的状况其实不错。我们预计会在第三季度实现盈利。

segments.textEn: And that comes from the success of the Roadster.
segments.textZh: 而那得益于 Roadster 的成功。

segments.textEn: Yeah, and the Roadster. Then we also have a powertrain supply business to Daimler as well for an electric Smart that we're doing with them.
segments.textZh: 对，还有 Roadster。然后我们也有一项向戴姆勒供应动力总成的业务，用于我们正与他们合作开发的一款电动 Smart。

segments.textEn: Make the Smart car an electric car?
segments.textZh: 把 Smart 汽车变成电动汽车？

segments.textEn: Yeah, you know, the Smart car was always intended to be an electric car, but they could never, they could never get the battery right. So a year and a half ago we met with Daimler and I was trying to convince them to work with us. I mean, we've really tried hard to work with a lot of different car companies.
segments.textZh: 对，你知道，Smart 汽车原本一直就是要做成电动汽车的，但他们始终无法，他们始终无法把电池做好。所以1年半前，我们与戴姆勒见了面，我当时试图说服他们与我们合作。我的意思是，我们确实非常努力地尝试与许多不同的汽车公司合作。

segments.textEn: And what happened?
segments.textZh: 然后发生了什么？

segments.textEn: Well, I guess they think, well, they took the attitude of what does some little startup in Silicon Valley know that we don't know or couldn't do?
segments.textZh: 嗯，我猜他们觉得，嗯，他们采取的态度是：硅谷的某家小型初创公司能知道什么我们不知道或做不到的东西？

segments.textEn: What would you say to them?
segments.textZh: 你会对他们说什么？

segments.textEn: Well, we drive our car and look at our technology and I don't know, it just never seemed to sort of sink in.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我们开我们的车，也看我们的技术，而我不知道，这似乎就是一直没能真正被理解。

segments.textEn: But
segments.textZh: 但是

segments.textEn: Daimler did actually. So I went through Stuttgart on the way to India actually and met with Dr. Weber, the head of Global R and D and we had a conversation. I said, well, what does it take for us to work together? We'd love to do something. We'd love to do something with an affordable mass market car that we ourselves could, couldn't do right now because we
segments.textZh: 戴姆勒确实这么做了。所以实际上我在前往印度的途中经过斯图加特，会见了全球研发部门负责人韦伯博士，我们进行了一番交谈。我说，那么，我们要怎样才能合作？我们很想做点什么。我们很想围绕一款价格亲民的大众市场汽车做点什么，而这件事目前靠我们自己能做、做不了，因为我们

segments.textEn: don't have the capability geared up to Zimmer line. Most of it.
segments.textZh: 没有为Zimmer生产线准备好相应的能力。其中大部分。

segments.textEn: Yeah. And so I said, what about electric Smart? Because the Smart was always intended to be an electric car and what would it take for us to work together? And he said, well, if you could do a prototype, that would really go a long way. So we did, we worked really hard. The powertrain team led by JB Straubel did an awesome job. And 40 days later when, when they came out to visit, we said, here's a car, take a drive.
segments.textZh: 是的。于是我说，电动Smart怎么样？因为Smart从一开始就打算成为一款电动汽车，要怎样我们才能合作？他说，嗯，如果你们能做出一辆原型车，那确实会大有帮助。所以我们做了，我们非常努力。由JB·斯特劳贝尔带领的动力总成团队做得非常出色。40天后，当、当他们前来参观时，我们说，车在这里，开开看吧。

segments.textEn: And they really liked what they saw.
segments.textZh: 他们非常喜欢自己看到的东西。

segments.textEn: And so what did they do then?
segments.textZh: 那么他们接着做了什么？

segments.textEn: They said, ok, well let's take it sort of another step further. And they gave us a little R and D contract and eventually got to the point where we got a contract to supply 1000 cars for them and then if we do well in that, we'll potentially go into tens of thousands of cars. But this is a car that everyone could afford and, and could hopefully come quite soon.
segments.textZh: 他们说，好吧，那么我们就把它再往前推进一步。他们给了我们一份小额研发合同，最后发展到我们拿到了一份为他们供应1000辆汽车的合同，然后，如果我们在这件事上做得好，就有可能进一步达到数万辆汽车。但这是一款所有人都买得起的汽车，而且、而且希望能很快问世。

segments.textEn: Do you have a profile of the people who you think will want to buy these roadsters?
segments.textZh: 对于你认为会想购买这些Roadster的人，你有一个用户画像吗？

segments.textEn: Yeah, absolutely. It's the kind of person who likes a performance car. Maybe they own a Porsche or Lamborghini or something.
segments.textZh: 有，当然有。就是那种喜欢高性能汽车的人。也许他们拥有一辆保时捷或兰博基尼之类的车。

segments.textEn: This car is actually faster than Lamborghini 00:60?
segments.textZh: 这辆车实际上比兰博基尼00:60还快？

segments.textEn: Yeah, I think faster than almost anything I know of. Yeah, I mean the really sort of million dollar supercars, obviously those will, those will beat it. Like the Ferrari Enzo is going to be faster, but it's pretty much faster than any normal sports car and it's really easy to drive. If you want a high performance car with a clean conscience, this is the only option the sedan is going to be for someone that wants a great sedan and also clean conscience.
segments.textZh: 是的，我觉得它比我所知道的几乎任何车都快。是的，我是说，那些真正意义上价值100万美元的超级跑车，显然它们会、它们会胜过它。比如法拉利Enzo会更快，但它差不多比任何普通跑车都快，而且非常容易驾驶。如果你想要一辆既有高性能又让良心清白的汽车，这是唯一的选择；这款轿车将面向那些既想要一辆出色轿车，也想让良心清白的人。

segments.textEn: And it's also going to be cheaper to operate than.
segments.textZh: 而且它的使用成本也会低于。

segments.textEn: You are, as you well know, a controversial guy as well.
segments.textZh: 你也很清楚，你也是一个有争议的人。

segments.textEn: I try to, I try not to be controversial but it seems, controversy seems to find me.
segments.textZh: 我尽量，我尽量不引发争议，但似乎，争议似乎总会找上我。

segments.textEn: It finds you. It finds you because you think big. You're a software guy who has been successful in the private sector.
segments.textZh: 它会找上你。它找上你，是因为你敢想大事。你是一个在私营领域取得了成功的软件人士。

segments.textEn: Yeah.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: You know, and see no reason you can't do things that other people have not been able to. No other how large the corporate enterprise. Create the best electric car or b put privately astronauts in space, which you say you will do in two years?
segments.textZh: 你知道，而且看不出有什么理由让你无法做到其他人没能做到的事。没有其他无论企业集团有多庞大。造出最好的电动汽车，或者b，以私人方式将宇航员送入太空，而你说你会在2年内做到？

segments.textEn: Well, yeah, it sort of depends on when NASA asks us to do that. So if NASA turns on access to do that this year, which we're hopeful that they will. The White House has a convene a panel on the future of human spaceflight that that panel is going to make the recommendations in a few months. I hope that some of those recommendations will be favorable to SpaceX because the alternative is if, if Space X doesn't do it, we will be entirely dependent on the Russians to carry our astronauts to the space station after 2010 and billions of dollars will be spent on essentially a sole source situation to the Russians, which I think is outrageous.
segments.textZh: 嗯，是的，这多少取决于NASA什么时候要求我们这么做。所以，如果NASA今年开放权限让我们这么做，而我们希望他们会这样做。白宫召集了一个关于载人航天未来的小组，那个小组将在几个月后提出建议。我希望其中一些建议会对SpaceX有利，因为另一种情况是，如果，如果SpaceX不做这件事，那么2010年之后，我们将完全依赖俄罗斯人把我们的宇航员送往空间站，并且会在实质上由俄罗斯人独家承接的局面上花费数十亿美元，我认为这令人愤慨。

segments.textEn: And you haven't taken advantage of the opportunity to go in space yourself, have you?
segments.textZh: 而你还没有利用这个机会亲自去太空，对吧？

segments.textEn: No, I have not.
segments.textZh: 不，我没有。

segments.textEn: Have you wanted to?
segments.textZh: 你想去吗？

segments.textEn: If it was purely a matter of personal interest, I would have done it already. I mean I do want it, I do want it.
segments.textZh: 如果纯粹是个人兴趣的问题，我早就已经去做了。我的意思是，我确实想去，我确实想去。

segments.textEn: Sergey interested in that or. No, Sergey has expressed some interest in that.
segments.textZh: 谢尔盖对此感兴趣，还是。不是，谢尔盖对此表达过一些兴趣。

segments.textEn: Some interest, yes.
segments.textZh: 有一些兴趣，是的。

segments.textEn: Yeah, I would like to go at some point, but it's. I'm also in the point where it's difficult for me to take personal risks. I used to take a lot of personal risks because of children. I've got my kids and responsibilities with companies as well. And so if I do things where they have personal risk, at this point, I risk more than my own being.
segments.textZh: 是的，我希望有一天能去，但这。我现在也处于一个很难让我承担个人风险的阶段。我过去会承担很多个人风险，因为孩子。我有孩子，还有对公司的责任。所以，如果我现在去做存在个人风险的事情，我拿来冒险的就不只是我自己。

segments.textEn: How many trips? You have one set of triptas and one set of twins.
segments.textZh: 多少次行程？你有一组特里普塔斯和一对双胞胎。

segments.textEn: Yeah, have the twins with me in New York, actually.
segments.textZh: 是的，其实双胞胎和我一起在纽约。

segments.textEn: So they like the car.
segments.textZh: 所以他们喜欢那辆车。

segments.textEn: Yeah. They can't drive. They can't go on the roadster because it doesn't. It's not very kid friendly. But no, it's not very different.
segments.textZh: 是的。他们不能开车。他们不能坐那辆Roadster，因为它不。它对孩子不是很友好。不过不，它并没有很不一样。

segments.textEn: You're right.
segments.textZh: 你说得对。

segments.textEn: The sedan will be ideal for them.
segments.textZh: 轿车会非常适合他们。

segments.textEn: Much success to you. Thank you for coming. Thank you for joining us. See you next time.
segments.textZh: 祝你取得巨大成功。谢谢你来。感谢你收看我们的节目。下次见。
